data: Humiliation: Power, Subjectivity, and Social Life

This course explores humiliation as both an intimate emotion and a powerful social force. Drawing on philosophy, psychoanalysis, ethnography, military and conflict studies, caste/race scholarship, and literature—with South Asia as a comparative anchor—students examine humiliation as a moral violation, psychological injury, tool of governance, structural condition, and literary motif. The course equips students with theoretical insight, ethnographic sensitivity, and ethical reflexivity while engaging with challenging histories and lived experiences.
Assistant Professor, Sociology and Social Anthropology
